To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the low-frequency vibrational properties and the dynamics of lysozymes are significantly affected by sugars.

(1) the low-frequency Raman susceptibility of lysozymes is dominated by vibrations of the protein backbone and side chains, (2) the low-frequency vibrational modes of lysozymee are softened in water, and (3) sugars stiffen the protein environment by increasing the strength of hydrogen bonds between water molecules.

the vibrational properties of proteins in sugar solutions are mainly governed by the influence of sugars on water dynamics and on the hydrogen bond network, which in turn affect the vibrational properties experienced by the atoms of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of low-frequency vibrational properties, i.e., the Raman susceptibility and the vibrational densities of state, of lysozymes in aqueous solutions containing three protecting sugars.

the study of the influence of the sugar concentration on the low-frequency vibrational properties, namely, the Raman spectra and the vibrational densities of state (VDOS), of lysozymes in sugar/water solutions.
the low-frequency vibrational properties, i.e., the Raman spectra and the vibrational density of states (VDos), of lysozymes in water and in sugar solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of sugars to lysozyme aqueous solutions induces the stiffening of the protein environment, the stiffening of water, and a slowing down of the water dynamics, all these effects counteracting the unfolding of the protein.
sugars stabilize proteins by slowing down the water dynamics and by strengthening the hydrogen bond network.
sugars stabilize the native structure of lysozymes by a combination of two effects, namely, the strengthening of the hydrogen bonds of water and the stiffening of the protein environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of sugars to the aqueous solution of lysozymes induces a slowing down of protein dynamics and a stiffening of the environment experienced by protein atoms, which are both responsible for the stabilization of proteins at high temperatures.

sugars induce a stiffening of the environment experienced by protein residues and a strengthening of the hydrogen bonding network of water, which may both counteract the protein softening upon unfolding and the water softening upon denaturation.

, in the case of lysozymes in sugar aqueous solution, the low-frequency vibrational properties reflect the dynamics of both water and lysozymes, and the sugar/water interactions, which are responsible for protein stabilization, induce a significant stiffening of the hydrogen bond networks of both protein and water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the low-frequency vibrational properties are a good tool for investigating protein dynamics and for understanding the mechanism of protein stabilization by sugars in aqueous solutions.

the vibrational properties of proteins and water in the lysozymes/sugar/water systems are strongly affected by sugars and that the Raman scattering technique is an efficient method to probe the protein and water dynamics in these complex systems.

sugars induce an overall stiffening of the protein environment that may counteract the destabilization of proteins at high temperatures, thereby providing an efficient protection against protein unfolding and aggregation.
